subject: Post-demo benchmark clarifications and A/B plan with hyperscaler
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@datasilo.com>, Ravi Menon <ravi.m@datasilo.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo benchmark clarifications and A/B plan with hyperscaler

Thanks for the demo time today — appreciate the open discussion, Emily and Ravi. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the lab scope and avoid back-and-forth:

Summary:
- Goal: quantify p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec for your most common inference paths and compare Redwood hosted + dedicated routing vs the hyperscaler endpoint you referenced.
- Workloads: short chat prompts (~128 tokens typical), mid-length summarization (~1k tokens), and long-context retrieval (~6k tokens). We should capture cold/warm KV-cache behavior.

Questions / asks from DataSilo:
1) Can you share a representative request trace and a small sample of payloads (anonymized)?
2) Are you okay with us running side-by-side A/B tests where we hit both endpoints from the same VPC/egress point?

Proposed test plan (attached: redwood-bench-config-v1.yaml):
- 3 runs per scenario, each run 10k requests distributed across seq lengths above.
- Report: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, median variance across runs, and detailed token-level breakdown for the 95/99 windows.
- Network metrics: capture e2e time (client->response) and server-side processing time where possible.

Timeline & owners:
- We can start the lab week of Sep 21. Marissa will own the Redwood lab execution; Ben will coordinate credits/contract items.

Attachments: redwood-bench-config-v1.yaml (config), post-demo-screencap.png (call notes).

Next steps:
- Emily/Ravi: share a 1–2GB anonymized sample and confirm you’re OK with the proposed test window for Sep 21–23.
- Marissa: confirm lab owner and baseline model variant (should we test quantized v2.1?).
- Ben: confirm any procurement touches and trial credit amount to propose.

I’ll schedule a 30-min sync to kick off once we have confirmation.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0167
From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@datasilo.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi.m@datasilo.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo benchmark clarifications and A/B plan with hyperscaler

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful. We can share an anonymized sample and a short trace; attached is a small workload slice (see notes). A few clarifications from our side: 

- We prefer side-by-side tests originating from our VPC to minimize network variance; Hyperscale can accept traffic from our subnet. Is Redwood comfortable with that?
- For long-context tests we need tokenization parity — we currently use a custom tokenizer shim. Can you run both endpoints through our tokenization or provide a checksum method so we compare apples-to-apples?
- Can you confirm whether your reported server-side processing time will include any prefix/KV cache warmup skew? We want to see both cold and warm windows clearly labeled.

Attachments: datasilo-sample-requests.tar.gz (3.2MB), datalog-excerpt-0901.json (logs).

Happy to proceed Sep 21–23 as long as you can accept tests from our VPC.

—
Emily Cho
Head of ML Ops | DataSilo Inc.
emily.cho@datasilo.com | +1 212-555-0189
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Cho <emily.cho@datasilo.com>, Ravi Menon <ravi.m@datasilo.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo benchmark clarifications and A/B plan with hyperscaler

Jordan / team — I can run the lab. Quick notes on the execution plan: 

- Lab owner: Marissa Cole (I’ll own the Redwood side runs and reporting).
- Model variant: agree to test quantized v2.1 and full-precision v2.1 so we can show quantization delta.
- Measurement approach: we’ll instrument both e2e and server-side processing time. For tokenization parity, we can run your tokenizer shim if DataSilo provides it; otherwise we’ll use a checksum approach to align token counts.
- Run cadence: do three independent trials per scenario (10k requests each) and report medians; we’ll surface per-run variance so you can see stability.

Ben — can you confirm trial credits (recommended: 200K tokens equivalent on Dedicated) and whether legal needs a one-page addendum to allow cross-endpoint testing from DataSilo’s VPC?

I’ll put together a short lab runbook and expected artifact set (raw traces, aggregated CSVs, p95/p99 graphs) and share by EOD Fri.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Cho <emily.cho@datasilo.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo benchmark clarifications and A/B plan with hyperscaler

Sounds good. I can approve a temporary trial credit package — recommending we offer 200K token credits on Dedicated plus a 10% professional services discount for the lab run to reduce friction.

Legal: I’ll loop in contracts but preliminarily a one-page addendum (test scope + liability cap) should suffice. Jordan — please flag if DataSilo needs an MSA amendment or full PO.

Timeline: I’ll have credits and draft addendum ready by Sep 20; Marissa, feel free to start with your lab runbook in parallel.

—

Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo benchmark clarifications and A/B plan with hyperscaler

Thanks everyone — aligned. Quick summary of agreed items and immediate actions: 

Agreed: 
- Side-by-side tests from DataSilo VPC Sep 21–23. Redwood will accept traffic from the provided subnet.
- Measurement: cold vs warm windows; tokenization parity via checksum shim (DataSilo to share if they want exact parity).
- Models: quantized v2.1 and FP v2.1. Three runs per scenario; artifacts: traces, CSVs, p95/p99 graphs.
- Commercial: 200K token trial on Dedicated + 10% PS discount; Ben to circulate addendum.

Immediate next steps: 
1) Emily/Ravi: send tokenization shim or confirm checksum method by EOD Mon (Sep 20).
2) Ben: share addendum draft and confirm credits on Sep 20.
3) Marissa: share lab runbook (expected artifacts + report template) by EOD Fri Sep 17 (attached link).
4) I’ll send a 30-min kickoff invite for Tue Sep 22, 10:00 AM PT and attach the config used for Redwood runs.

Link to HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DS-2026-457

Looking forward — Jordan
